ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The ancient Greek mathematician Eratosthenes came up with an ingenious idea to measure the circumference of the Earth. Eratosthenes lived in Alexandria, and 785 kilometers due south of this city, there was a city Syene on the same meridian (30°E) as Alexandria. At 12 noon on the summer solstice, while sunlight shone directly onto the bottom of a dry well in the city of Syene, Eratosthenes used a wooden pole and a protractor in Alexandria to accurately calculate the circumference of the Earth (∠1 in the figure is 7.2°). <image1> According to the material and the diagram, what is the circumference of the Earth calculated by Eratosthenes, in kilometers?
